document.title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
document.author: Satoshi Nakamoto

claims.label: Peer-to-peer electronic cash
claims.statement: Online payments can be sent directly from one party to another without going through a financial institution.
claims.notes: This is a founding objective, not a single consensus rule. ORIGIN records architectural evidence rather than declaring a binary verdict.

claims.label: No trusted third party for double-spend prevention
claims.statement: The network addresses double-spending through a peer-to-peer proof-of-work timestamp chain.

claims.label: Hash-based proof-of-work history
claims.statement: Transactions are timestamped into an ongoing proof-of-work chain whose history becomes increasingly costly to alter.

claims.label: Independent verification
claims.statement: Participants can verify transactions and proof-of-work without relying on a central authority.

claims.label: Economic incentive
claims.statement: Block rewards and transaction fees align network participation with honest operation.

claims.label: Most accumulated proof-of-work
claims.statement: The accepted history is represented by the chain with the greatest accumulated proof-of-work.
